tax.bar <- df.rpt |> 
  group_by(Isolate) |> 
  filter(taxRank %in% c('U', 'P')) |> 
  mutate(taxon = if_else(percentage < 5, 'Other', clean_taxon(name))) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_col(aes(x = percentage, y = Isolate, fill = taxon), position = 'fill') +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = library.labels) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = taxon_palette) +
  labs(x = "Reads (%)", y = NULL, fill = "Taxon")
save_pub_r(tax.bar, 'taxonomy-composition-bar', width_mm = 180, height_mm = 100)
tax.bar

Can GC content and coverage separate target Oomycota reads from contamination?

Per-read GC content (seqkit fx2tab) and per-read 21-mer self-coverage (KAT sect) for the adapter-filtered HiFi reads of all three new isolates (MSU1, SC1982, Phumuli), colored by the same Kraken2 phylum-level taxon call used for the read-composition panel above (taxRank %in% c('U','P'), phyla below 5% of a library’s reads collapsed to “Other”). This is the read-level analogue of a blobtools blob plot: assembly-level GC/coverage is not informative here because most of these libraries are pre-assembly and dominated by non-target DNA (see the taxonomic composition above), so the question is asked directly of the reads.

Coverage is per-read median 21-mer depth from KAT sect in self-comparison mode (each read’s own k-mers scored against the k-mer spectrum of the full read set) - a proxy for how many times that piece of the underlying genome/molecule was sampled, not a per-base assembly coverage. Points are a stratified random subsample (up to 3,000 reads per isolate x category) for plotting; category summary statistics (data/blobplot-category-summary-by-isolate.tsv) are computed from the full read sets.

plot_data <- read_tsv(
  here("data", "blobplot-read-coverage-gc-subsample.tsv"),
  col_types = cols(
    isolate = col_character(),
    read_id = col_character(),
    category = col_character(),
    gc_pct = col_double(),
    cov_median = col_double()
  )
) |>
  mutate(Isolate = factor(recode(isolate, !!!isolate.labels), levels = isolate.labels))

blob.plot <- plot_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x = gc_pct, y = cov_median, color = category)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.25, size = 0.4) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  scale_color_manual(values = taxon_palette) +
  facet_wrap(~Isolate, nrow = 1) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1, size = 1.2))) +
  labs(x = "GC content (%)", y = "Median 21-mer coverage", color = "Taxon")

save_pub_r(blob.plot, "blobplot-coverage-gc", width_mm = 180, height_mm = 71)
blob.plot

Finding

Coverage separates some categories better than GC content does - e.g. Pseudomonadota and Bacteroidota sit at consistently low coverage relative to the rest of each library - but neither axis, nor the combination, cleanly separates target Oomycota reads from contamination. Oomycota does not form a single distinct cluster in any of the three panels: it spans essentially the whole coverage range visible in each isolate, overlapping heavily with Streptophyta (host), Other and unclassified. Conversely, every visually distinct cloud/band in the plot is a mixture of taxa rather than a pure category. GC content alone is close to uninformative for this separation (categories overlap almost completely on the x-axis in all three isolates). A blob-plot-style GC/coverage view, at either the assembly or the read level, is not sufficient here to distinguish target genome reads from contaminant or host reads.
